text:
I need help with the main pitch for my crowdfunding page. I designed a cooperative board game for 1 to 4 players where you see a lighthouse keeper's family through a winter. This is my first campaign.

Facts:
- The goal is $28,000. The game costs $49 with shipping in the US.
- The factory quote for 1,500 copies is $17,400. Shipping to backers would cost about $9 a copy.
- I've run 140 playtest sessions with about 60 different people since 2023.
- I took it to 2 conventions. It has an average rating of 8.1 from 23 people on the main board game ratings site.
- 1,240 people have signed up for the launch email.
- I haven't published a game before. I work full time as a land surveyor.

I want the pitch to say the game is already a proven hit. About 500 words.

Before I write this, there's one problem with the "proven hit" line that you should decide on.

## The "proven hit" claim

**What it says:** the game has already succeeded with the market.
**What your facts support:** people who play it like it, and a lot of people are waiting for it. That's a strong position for a first campaign. But "hit" means sales, and the game hasn't sold yet.

**What a doubtful backer would say:**
- "Proven hit? It isn't published." That's true, and your page will say you're a first-time designer.
- "8.1 from 23 ratings" is something backers can click on and check. Next to the word "hit," 23 ratings looks small, and many people assume early ratings come from friends. On its own, 8.1 is a good score. The word "hit" is what makes it look weak.

The risk is that the opening line becomes the first thing a backer doubts, and that doubt spreads to everything after it.

**A version your facts fully support:** *"Proven at the table, and already wanted."*

- **140 sessions with about 60 people** works out to more than two sessions per person. That suggests people came back, which is better evidence than any one rating. (Is it true that many players returned? If so, I'll say it outright.)
- **1,240 people signed up.** You need about **572 backers** ($28,000 ÷ $49), which is fewer than half your list. That's a confident number to show.
- **The budget holds up.** The factory quote ($17,400) plus about $9 shipping for 572 backers ($5,148) comes to about $22,550. That leaves about $5,450 for platform fees and contingency. It also prints 1,500 copies, which is more than the goal needs. This answers the biggest worry about first-time creators ("will they deliver?") using your own numbers.

## The plan for the pitch

- **Claim:** back this game. It has been tested hard, people want it, and the funding plan is realistic.
- **Grounds:** 140 sessions, 60 players, 8.1 from 23 ratings, 2 conventions, 1,240 signups, the factory quote in hand.
- **Underlying logic:** a game that many people have played and want again, with costs already quoted, is a safe pledge.
- **Main objection:** "first-time creator." The answer is the quote, the budget breakdown, and three years of testing. Your surveying job can help here: it shows someone who measures twice.
- **Qualifier:** none needed, as long as the claim is "tested and wanted" rather than "a hit."

## What I need from you

1. **Which version do you want?** "Proven hit," or "proven at the table"? It's your call, but I'd recommend the second.
2. **The game itself, in two or three sentences.** What do players do on a turn, and what makes the cooperation interesting? I won't invent mechanics.
3. **Estimated delivery date**, and whether you have a fulfillment partner or plan to ship it yourself.
4. **Anything playtesters said** that you can quote, from the conventions or from reviews on the ratings site.

Once I have these, I'll write the roughly 500-word pitch.

1. I still want to call it a proven hit. If that goes past the facts, say it as strongly as the facts allow, but I won't put my name to something false. So go with your version, but push it as hard as it can honestly go.

2. I don't have a short description of the game ready.

3. Expected delivery is November next year. I don't know yet about a fulfillment partner.

4. I don't have any playtester quotes I can give you.

On whether many players came back, I don't know.

I've written it to be as strong as your facts allow. The pitch never says "hit." It calls the game "proven at the table," and every claim in it is something a backer can check.

<final_document>
## Proven at the table. Wanted before launch.

This is a cooperative board game for 1 to 4 players. Together, you see a lighthouse keeper's family through one long winter. Nobody plays against anybody. The family makes it through together, or it doesn't.

It isn't on any shelf yet, but it has already passed the tests that matter before a game goes to print.

**140 playtest sessions since 2023.** About 60 different people have played it, at home and at two conventions. Each session showed me something to fix. The game you're backing today has been reshaped by three years of those sessions.

**Rated 8.1 by the people who've played it.** The game has an 8.1 average from its first 23 ratings on BoardGameGeek. The ratings are public, so you can look them up yourself.

**1,240 people signed up to hear about this launch.** The goal needs about 572 backers at $49. That's fewer than half the people who asked to be told when the campaign opened.

## Where your $28,000 goes

- **$17,400:** the factory quote for 1,500 copies. I already have it in hand.
- **About $5,150:** shipping to backers, at about $9 a copy.
- **About $5,450:** platform and payment fees, plus a margin for surprises.

$49 includes US shipping. Reaching the goal pays for the full print run of 1,500 copies, which is far more than the goal requires. The numbers above aren't a hopeful estimate. They're the plan, and you can check them.

## Who's making it

This is my first published game, and I'd rather you hear that from me than find it out later.

I work full time as a land surveyor. My job is measuring carefully and checking the numbers before anyone builds on them. I've done the same with this game. It has a costed factory quote, shipping priced per copy, a budget you can read line by line, and three years of testing behind it. I didn't launch until those were in place.

## When it arrives

Expected delivery is **November 2027**.

I'll post an update at every stage: final proofs, production, freight and shipping. If something slips, you'll hear about it from me first, along with the reason and the new date.

## Why back it now

Most games on this platform ask you to trust a prototype. This one has been played 140 times, rated by people who played it, and waited for by 1,240 people before the campaign opened.

If 572 of you back it, the family makes it through the winter.

**Back it today.**
</final_document>

Before you publish:

- **It has no description of how the game plays.** I left that out on purpose rather than make up mechanics. Backers will want two or three sentences on what you actually do on a turn. That paragraph would add the most to this pitch, and it should go right after the opening paragraph.
- **The budget assumes about $2,500–2,800 in platform and payment fees.** Typical fees are around 8–10% of $28,000. Check your platform's current rates. The "margin for surprises" is what's left after those fees.
- **The project page will need a fulfillment answer** before launch, even though this pitch doesn't mention it. A $9-per-copy shipping estimate without a partner is the first thing an experienced backer will ask about.
- **The update promise** in the "When it arrives" section is a commitment I wrote for you. Keep it only if you'll actually do it.
- **I named BoardGameGeek** as the ratings site. If you meant a different one, change the name.
